rules.completion_test: For each skeleton, replacing every open step by a proof makes the final Collatz statement follow by the displayed dependency chain.
rules.citation_test: Every term and claimed input in a step is pinned to a canonical item ID; canonical items carry source paths and literature IDs in data/items.json.
rules.nonredundancy_test: A route is retained only if its remaining gate or proof architecture is not merely a special case or representation of another retained route.

skeletons.name: Terminal synchronization plus cycle integrality
skeletons.sufficiency: Closing OPEN-BTS-01 and OPEN-CYCLE-INT-01 proves the full Collatz conjecture.

steps.formal_statement: For every word-realized accelerated odd orbit, 2^{A_k}x_k=3^k x_0+C_k, with the strict-barrier and target-dual definitions fixed by DEF-U-01 and DEF-WORD-01.
steps.lean_style: theorem affine_iterate (x : OddPos) (a : ValuationWord) (k : Nat) (hk : k ≤ a.length) : 2^(partialA a k) * orbit x k = 3^k * x + carryAt a k := by ...

steps.formal_statement: If Collatz is false, choose the least positive odd n that does not reach 1. Its orbit never drops below n; because U is deterministic on integers, that orbit is either unbounded or eventually enters a nontrivial cycle.
steps.lean_style: theorem least_counterexample_dichotomy (h : ¬ Collatz) : ∃ n : OddPos, MinimalBad n ∧ (UnboundedOrbit U n ∨ EntersNontrivialCycle U n) := by ...

steps.formal_statement: Every unbounded positive orbit has a tail whose valuation word is an infinite strict barrier and whose coefficient surplus tends to infinity; the nested dyadic cylinder representatives of a fixed ordinary seed eventually stabilize to that seed.
steps.lean_style: theorem normalize_unbounded (n : OddPos) (h : UnboundedOrbit U n) : ∃ tail : BarrierRay, SurplusTendsToInfinity tail ∧ EventuallyConstantLeastLift tail := by ...

steps.formal_statement: At consecutive coefficient tail records j_i of a normalized unbounded ray, either r_i>R_4(x_{j_i}), in which case r_i>=6 and v_3(x_{j_{i+1}}+1)<=r_i-5, or the gap word is one of {1,12,1113,1122}. Hence every ray has infinitely many horizon exits, unbounded runs of the one-letter atom inside the horizons, or an eventually bounded decoder. Canonical decoder ancestors tend to infinity; with finite stationary height K, their decoder depths and one-letter run lengths satisfy the explicit record-index budgets in THM-DIV-RECORD-RENEWAL-01.
steps.lean_style: theorem record_horizon_trichotomy (ray : NormalizedUnboundedRay) : InfinitelyManyHorizonExits ray ∨ UnboundedOneAtomRuns ray ∨ EventuallyBoundedDecoder ray := by ...

steps.formal_statement:
Assume that \(n\) is the least positive odd integer with an unbounded accelerated orbit. Fix a finite segment of that orbit. The least same-depth predecessor of its endpoint is already classified and gives no new start below \(n\). Every longer predecessor factors into an inverse prefix and a same-depth suffix. The formerly possible suffix start \(q+2\) is impossible; the unresolved nonminimal suffixes are the actual \(q\)-suffix when the local half-seed is smaller and the positive-defect starts

\[
r\ge2^\delta q-\frac{2^\delta-(-1)^\delta}{3}.
\]

If the prefix has length \(h\) and exponent sum \(\operatorname B(E)\), put \(t:=\operatorname B(E)-h\). The cases \(t=0,1,2,3\) are classified by finite valuation ladders, and every prefix satisfies the sharp interval

\[
2^t\left(\left(\frac23\right)^h(r+1)-\frac23\right)-\frac13\le z\le\left(\frac23\right)^h(2^t r+1)-1.
\]

Writing the exponents as \(1+c_i\) and \(p_k=\sum_{i\le k}c_i\), exact carry-position identities now impose a simultaneous finite power-of-two screen on every \(p_k\). Prove that every deep prefix passing all of these screens and every unresolved suffix starts at least at \(n\), or construct a positive odd start \(z<n\) whose orbit merges into the orbit of \(n\). The horizon-exit and eventual reset alternatives must also be excluded.
steps.lean_style: theorem binary_ternary_stabilization (n : OddPos) (hmin : GloballyLeastUnbounded n) : ExistsHorizonExitCanonicalAncestorBelow n ∨ ExistsInteriorNoncanonicalAncestorBelow n := by -- OPEN

steps.formal_statement: TSC-02, TSC-03, TSC-03R, and TSC-04 contradict global leastness of an unbounded seed: either alternative in TSC-04 supplies a smaller positive odd seed whose orbit reaches the same unbounded tail. Hence no positive orbit is unbounded.
steps.lean_style: theorem no_unbounded_of_stabilization (hBTS : BinaryTernaryStabilization) : ∀ n : OddPos, ¬ UnboundedOrbit U n := by ...

steps.formal_statement: Every nontrivial positive cycle produces a primitive strict-record valuation word a with A=ceil(r log_2 3), D=2^A-3^r>0, and D dividing C(a).
steps.lean_style: theorem cycle_to_integral_word (c : NontrivialCycle U) : ∃ a : ValuationWord, PrimitiveStrictRecordOneStrip a ∧ determinant a ∣ carry a := by ...

steps.formal_statement: No nontrivial primitive strict-record one-strip word satisfies (2^A-3^r) | C(a); equivalently, its reduced rational-cycle denominator q is greater than 1.
steps.lean_style: theorem cycle_integrality_obstruction (a : ValuationWord) (h : PrimitiveStrictRecordOneStrip a) (hnontrivial : ¬ TrivialWord a) : ¬ determinant a ∣ carry a := by -- OPEN

steps.formal_statement: TSC-06 and TSC-07 exclude every nontrivial positive cycle.
steps.lean_style: theorem no_nontrivial_cycles (hInt : CycleIntegralityObstruction) : ∀ c, ¬ NontrivialCycle U c := by intro c hc; obtain ⟨a, ha, hdiv⟩ := cycle_to_integral_word ⟨c,hc⟩; exact hInt a ha.1 ha.2 hdiv

steps.formal_statement: With unbounded orbits and nontrivial cycles excluded, the least-counterexample dichotomy is impossible; therefore every positive integer reaches 1.
steps.lean_style: theorem collatz_of_BTS_and_integrality (hBTS : BinaryTernaryStabilization) (hInt : CycleIntegralityObstruction) : Collatz := by by_contra h; obtain ⟨n,hn,hunb | hcyc⟩ := least_counterexample_dichotomy h; exact (no_unbounded_of_stabilization hBTS n) hunb; exact (no_nontrivial_cycles hInt _ ) hcyc

skeletons.name: Stationary inverse-fiber extinction
skeletons.sufficiency: Closing OPEN-FIBER-EXT-01 proves the full Collatz conjecture by strong induction.
skeletons.warning: The open gate is equivalent to Collatz. The finite-envelope and Bellman results organize the obstruction but do not currently weaken it.

steps.formal_statement: For positive odd n and r, define M_r(n)=min{z positive odd : U^r(z)=U^r(n)}; the set is nonempty because it contains n.
steps.lean_style: noncomputable def fiberMin (n : OddPos) (r : Nat) : OddPos := sInf {z | iterate U r z = iterate U r n}

steps.formal_statement: At each fixed depth, M_r(n) is obtained from a finite exact family of ancestor scores satisfying congruence, positivity, and valuation conditions, and the minima obey the nested Bellman decomposition M_{R+1}=min(M_R,Theta_R).
steps.lean_style: theorem fiberMin_finite_envelope (n : OddPos) (r : Nat) : fiberMin n r = Finset.min' (feasibleScores n r) (feasibleScores_nonempty n r) := by ...

steps.formal_statement: For every positive odd n>1, some finite depth r satisfies M_r(n)<n.
steps.lean_style: theorem stationary_inverse_fiber_extinction : ∀ n : OddPos, 1 < n → ∃ r : Nat, fiberMin n r < n := by -- OPEN

steps.formal_statement: Assume INV-03. By strong induction on odd n, choose z=M_r(n)<n with U^r(z)=U^r(n). The induction hypothesis makes z reach 1, so n reaches the same endpoint and then 1. Hence Collatz holds.
steps.lean_style: theorem collatz_of_fiber_extinction (hExt : StationaryInverseFiberExtinction) : Collatz := by intro n; induction n using Nat.strong_induction_on with | h n ih => by_cases h1 : n=1; · simp [h1]; · obtain ⟨r,z,hz,heq⟩ := hExt n (by omega); exact reachesOne_of_coalesces heq (ih z hz)

skeletons.name: Cycle descent plus exclusion of unbounded orbits
skeletons.sufficiency: Closing OPEN-FCD-01 and OPEN-HSCI-01 excludes respectively all nontrivial cycles and all divergent orbits, hence proves Collatz.

steps.formal_statement: If Collatz is false, a least odd counterexample has an orbit that is either unbounded or eventually enters a nontrivial cycle.
steps.lean_style: theorem least_counterexample_dichotomy (h : ¬ Collatz) : ∃ n : OddPos, MinimalBad n ∧ (UnboundedOrbit U n ∨ EntersNontrivialCycle U n) := by ...

steps.formal_statement: At the first shortcut-coefficient crossing of a least-state nontrivial integer cycle, the least state is the canonical dyadic representative rho and its endpoint Z satisfies Z>=rho.
steps.lean_style: theorem cycle_first_crossing_localization (c : NontrivialCycle U) : ∃ w, NonboundaryFirstCrossing w ∧ canonicalStart w = leastState c ∧ canonicalEndpoint w ≥ canonicalStart w := by ...

steps.formal_statement: Every nonboundary coefficient first-crossing word satisfies rho(w)>Z(w).
steps.lean_style: theorem first_crossing_descent (w : ShortcutWord) (h : NonboundaryFirstCrossing w) : canonicalStart w > canonicalEndpoint w := by -- OPEN

steps.formal_statement: FH-02 and FH-03 give opposite strict inequalities at the first crossing, so no nontrivial positive cycle exists.
steps.lean_style: theorem no_cycles_of_FCD (hFCD : FirstCrossingDescent) : ∀ c, ¬ NontrivialCycle U c := by ...

steps.formal_statement: Every unbounded orbit normalizes to an infinite strict-barrier ray with unbounded surplus and an eventually constant ordinary binary lift.
steps.lean_style: theorem unbounded_to_HSCI_counterexample (n : OddPos) (h : UnboundedOrbit U n) : ∃ w : BarrierRay, UnboundedSurplus w ∧ EventuallyConstantOrdinaryLift w := by ...

steps.formal_statement: Every normalized hypothetical divergent orbit has infinitely many deficit-four horizon exits at consecutive coefficient records, or it has a tail on which 1<e_j<=41/3, 2<=ceil(e_j)<=14, every ceiling defect lies in {-2,-1,0,1,2,3,4,5,6,7}, and the logarithmic separation clock at the ith coefficient record is at least i log(9/8)-O(1).
steps.lean_style: theorem record_companion_dichotomy (ray : NormalizedUnboundedRay) : InfinitelyManyHorizonExits ray ∨ EventuallyBoundedCompanionWithLinearClock ray := by ...

steps.formal_statement: In the interior alternative of FH-05R, let omega be the record-atom word over {1,12,1113,1122}. If an atom factor V repeats at record positions i<k, then 2^{B(V)+1} divides the difference of the two starting states and 2*3^{r(V)} divides the difference of the two terminal states. Hence B(V)+1<log_2(KQ_{j_0})+(log_2 3-1)k and liminf p_omega(L)/L>=1/(log_2 3-1). If every run of the atom 1 has length at most M, the lower complexity slope is at least (1+2/(M+1))/(log_2 3-1).
steps.lean_style: theorem record_atom_fixed_seed_spacing (ray : InteriorRecordAtomRay) : ReturnLattice ray /\ AtomComplexityFloor ray := by ...

steps.formal_statement: The interior alternative of FH-05R splits exhaustively. If C=1113 occurs infinitely often, every C transition x->y has x=79 mod 128 and admits z=(x-1)/2 with exact word 1121 and U_+^4(z)=y; its synchronized value is e_z=(e_x+1)/2 and z+e_z=(x+e_x)/2. On the orbit of a globally least positive odd unbounded seed n, every such occurrence satisfies x>=2n+1 and Q>2(n+1)/K. If C occurs only finitely often, then after its last occurrence there are infinitely many decoder-zero resets. Consecutive reset blocks are A^kB or A^kD and, for Y=2^nu u, obey respectively Y'=(3^nu u+1)/2 with Q'/Q=3^nu/2^{nu+1}, or Y'=(3^{nu+1}u+7)/8 with Q'/Q=3^{nu+1}/2^{nu+3}; moreover nu<=(log_2 3-1)i+log_2(KQ_{j_0}).
steps.lean_style: theorem record_atom_branching (ray : InteriorRecordAtomRay) : InfinitelyManyHalfCoalescences ray / EventuallyExactTwoMapResetRenewal ray := by ...

steps.formal_statement: In the infinite-C alternative of FH-05T, let b=v_3(x+1) at a C transition x->y. For every 0<=s<=b, z_s+1=2^{s-1}(x+1)/3^s has exact word 1^s1121 to y and z_s+epsilon_s=2^{s-1}(x+e_x)/3^s, forcing Q>[2(n+1)/K](3/2)^s on a globally least unbounded ray. The ladder pulls back exactly through a preceding run A^r. At the first preceding nontrivial atom it is blocked: a B/D endpoint makes the pulled-back half-seed divisible by 3, while across a preceding C from q the least four-step ancestor is 4q-1>q, uniquely with word 1215. Hence the direct half-seed ladder cannot itself be propagated to the fixed initial seed across a nontrivial record atom.
steps.lean_style: theorem C_decoder_ladder_blocker (ray : InteriorRecordAtomRay) : CDecoderLadder ray /\ DirectHalfPullbackBlockedAtNontrivialAtom ray := by ...

steps.formal_statement: Every exact block BA^rC or DA^rC has its actual start as the unique least same-depth inverse of its endpoint. The inverse mass minimum is respectively r+9 with reverse word (3,1^{r+3},2,1), and r+12 with reverse word (3,1^{r+3},2,2,1,1). Hence crossing one reset blocker before a C half-coalescence cannot descend at the same raw depth; a viable inverse branch must change depth or span at least two nontrivial record atoms.
steps.lean_style: theorem reset_C_same_depth_minimum (ray : InteriorRecordAtomRay) : OneResetSameDepthInverseMinimal ray := by ...

steps.formal_statement: For every P,Q in {B,C,D} and r,s>=0, let W=P A^r Q A^s C be an exact block with start q and endpoint y. Among all positive odd same-depth predecessors of y, the unique least one is q when P is B or D, while for P=C it is (q-1)/2 with initial replacement 1113->1121. The latter is only the already classified local half-seed at the earlier C. Hence a pullback based on the terminal C gives no new same-depth descent across its two preceding nontrivial atoms; after removing the local earlier-C alternative, a viable inverse branch must change raw depth or cross at least three preceding nontrivial atoms.
steps.lean_style: theorem two_prefix_same_depth_minimum (ray : InteriorRecordAtomRay) : TwoPrefixSameDepthInverseClassified ray := by ...

steps.formal_statement: For every exact finite record-atom word W=P U of raw depth L, with P in {B,C,D}, U in {A,B,C,D}*, start q, and endpoint y, the unique least positive odd L-step predecessor of y is q when P=B or D, and (q-1)/2 when P=C. In the C case the unique minimum word is 1121 U, exactly the local half-branch followed by the unchanged suffix. The proof propagates the aligned distortion state through an arbitrary number of atoms and establishes the uniform strip Delta>=-1, -1<=c/2^Delta<=5, with exact half-state rigidity at Delta=-1. Hence no finite same-depth pullback across any number of record atoms can create a new descent; the infinite-C branch now requires a different raw inverse depth.
steps.lean_style: theorem arbitrary_prefix_same_depth_minimum (ray : InteriorRecordAtomRay) : ArbitraryPrefixSameDepthInverseClassified ray := by ...

steps.formal_statement:
Every exact \((L+h)\)-step predecessor factors as an \(h\)-step prefix followed by one of three same-depth suffix cases: the local half case, a start in \(\{q,q+2\}\), or a start at least \(2^\delta(q-1)\) for some \(\delta\ge1\). If the prefix word is \(E\), put \(t:=\operatorname B(E)-h\). The excess-zero and excess-one prefixes are classified completely by explicit \(3\)-adic valuations. For \(0\le h\le v_3(q_*+1)\), the unique least longer predecessor is

\[
z_h+1=\left(\frac23\right)^h(q_*+1).
\]
steps.lean_style: theorem variable_depth_channel_and_decoder_reduction (ray : InteriorRecordAtomRay) : VariableDepthReducedToHigherExcessOrNonminimalSuffix ray := by ...

steps.formal_statement:
At every fixed positive odd suffix start \(r\), the exact inverse prefixes of excess two are precisely the two finite valuation families

\[
1^\ell3\,1^k,\qquad 1^{j-1}2\,1^{b_1-1}2\,1^b.
\]

Their starts and allowed ranges are explicit. No other excess-two word exists. Consequently there is a computable finite horizon \(H_{\le2}(r)\) beyond which every exact prefix has excess at least three.
steps.lean_style: theorem complete_excess_two_decoder (r : OddPos) : ExcessTwoPrefixesAreTwoFiniteValuationFamilies r := by ...

steps.formal_statement:
At every fixed positive odd suffix start \(r\), the exact inverse prefixes of excess three belong to exactly four finite valuation families, with word shapes

\[
1^{j-1}4\,1^b,\qquad 1^{j-1}2\,1^c3\,1^k,\qquad 1^\ell3\,1^k2\,1^b,\qquad 1^{j-1}2\,1^{b_2-1}2\,1^{b_1-1}2\,1^b.
\]

Consequently there is an explicit finite horizon \(H_{\le3}(r)\) beyond which every exact prefix has excess at least four.
steps.lean_style: theorem complete_excess_three_decoder (r : OddPos) : ExcessThreePrefixesAreFourFiniteValuationFamilies r := by ...

steps.formal_statement:
If an exact \(h\)-step prefix of excess \(t\) runs from \(z\) to \(r\), then

\[
2^t\left(\left(\frac23\right)^h(r+1)-\frac23\right)-\frac13\le z\le\left(\frac23\right)^h(2^t r+1)-1.
\]

Both endpoints are sharp. Hence every positive inverse prefix satisfies

\[
t\ge\max\left\{0,\left\lceil\log_2\left(\frac{2(3/2)^h-1}{r}\right)\right\rceil\right\},
\]

and any prefix with \(t\ge3\) that begins below a threshold \(N\) must lie beyond

\[
h>\log_{3/2}\left(\frac{24(q_*+1)}{3N+17}\right).
\]
steps.lean_style: theorem sharp_prefix_interval (E : ExponentWord) (hE : ExactPrefix E) : SharpCarryInterval E := by ...

steps.formal_statement: Let \(W=PU\), with \(P\in\{B,C,D\}\), be an exact record-atom word from \(q\) to \(y\). No exact word of the same length and mass runs from \(q+2\) to \(y\). Hence the same-depth suffix start is the local half-seed, the actual start \(q\), or a positive-defect value \(r\ge2^\delta(q-1)\) with \(\delta\ge1\). The formerly possible zero-defect value \(q+2\) is eliminated.
steps.lean_style: theorem q_plus_two_suffix_impossible (W : RecordAtomWord) (hW : Exact W q y) : ¬ SameDepthSameMassPath (q + 2) y W.length W.mass := by ...

steps.formal_statement:
For a same-depth suffix of positive mass defect \(\delta\ge1\), the suffix start satisfies the Jacobsthal bound

\[
r\ge2^\delta q-J_\delta,
\qquad
J_\delta:=\frac{2^\delta-(-1)^\delta}{3}.
\]

The proof extends the lower distortion strip to the phase immediately after the first exponent of each nontrivial record atom. Consequently, a prefix of length \(h\), excess \(t\ge T\), and start below the least unbounded seed \(n\) must satisfy

\[
h>\log_{3/2}\left(\frac{2^\delta q-J_\delta+1}{2/3+(n+1/3)/2^T}\right).
\]
steps.lean_style: theorem jacobsthal_positive_defect_suffix_bound (F : SameDepthSuffix W) (hdelta : 1 ≤ F.mass - W.mass) : F.start ≥ 2^F.defect * q - jacobsthal F.defect := by ...

steps.formal_statement:
Let \(E=(1+c_1,\ldots,1+c_h)\) be an exact inverse prefix from \(z\) to \(r\). Put \(t=\sum_i c_i\) and \(p_k=\sum_{i\le k}c_i\). The slack from each endpoint of the sharp interval is exactly

\[
U_{h,t}(r)-z=\frac13\sum_{k=1}^{h-1}\left(\frac23\right)^k(2^{p_k}-1),
\]

\[
z-L_{h,t}(r)=\frac13\sum_{k=1}^{h-1}\left(\frac23\right)^k(2^t-2^{p_k}).
\]

Hence a proposed bounded start must pass an explicit simultaneous power-of-two screen for every cumulative excess \(p_k\).
steps.lean_style: theorem carry_position_squeeze (E : ExponentWord) (hE : ExactPrefix E) : ExactEndpointSlack E ∧ CumulativeExcessScreen E := by ...

steps.formal_statement:
Assume that \(n\) is the least positive odd integer with an unbounded accelerated orbit. For the branch containing infinitely many occurrences of the word \(1113\), prove that every remaining variable-depth competitor starts at least at \(n\), or construct one that starts below \(n\). The value \(q+2\) is already impossible. The unresolved suffixes are the actual \(q\)-suffix when it is nonminimal and the positive-defect starts

\[
r\ge2^\delta q-\frac{2^\delta-(-1)^\delta}{3}.
\]

The unresolved prefixes include the deep minimum-channel range beyond \(H_{\le3}(r)\). Every such prefix must obey the sharp interval

\[
2^t\left(\left(\frac23\right)^h(r+1)-\frac23\right)-\frac13\le z\le\left(\frac23\right)^h(2^t r+1)-1.
\]

In particular, a competitor with \(t\ge3\) and \(z<n\) must satisfy

\[
h>\log_{3/2}\left(\frac{24(q_*+1)}{3n+17}\right).
\]

Moreover, if the exponent excesses are \(c_i\) and \(p_k=\sum_{i\le k}c_i\), then every surviving deep prefix must satisfy the exact carry-position screen at every \(1\le k<h\). The remaining task is to show that no deep triple passes all of these coupled constraints below \(n\), or to turn a survivor into the required smaller merging start.

The alternative with only finitely many occurrences of \(1113\), and the separate horizon-exit alternative, also remain to be excluded. Closing all three alternatives rules out unbounded positive orbits. No claim about nontrivial cycles is made here.
steps.lean_style: theorem high_surplus_carry_innovation (ray : NormalizedBarrierRay) (hfix : EventuallyConstantOrdinaryLift ray) : ¬ InfinitelyManyHorizonExits ray ∧ (ExistsSmallerHalfCoalescingSeed ray ∨ ¬ EventuallyExactTwoMapResetRenewal ray) := by -- OPEN

steps.formal_statement: FH-05 and FH-06 exclude every unbounded positive orbit.
steps.lean_style: theorem no_unbounded_of_HSCI (hHSCI : HighSurplusCarryInnovation) : ∀ n : OddPos, ¬ UnboundedOrbit U n := by ...

steps.formal_statement: With FH-04 and FH-07, both alternatives in FH-01 are impossible, so every positive integer reaches 1.
steps.lean_style: theorem collatz_of_FCD_HSCI (hFCD : FirstCrossingDescent) (hHSCI : HighSurplusCarryInnovation) : Collatz := by by_contra h; obtain ⟨n,hn,hunb | hcyc⟩ := least_counterexample_dichotomy h; exact no_unbounded_of_HSCI hHSCI n hunb; exact no_cycles_of_FCD hFCD _ hcyc

skeletons.name: Mixed binary-ternary rewrite termination
skeletons.sufficiency: Closing OPEN-REWRITE-RELTERM-01 proves termination of the full Yolcu-Aaronson-Heule rewrite system; their simulation theorem then proves the ordinary Collatz conjecture.
skeletons.warning: The residual relative-termination gate is equivalent to Collatz. This skeleton is retained as an operationally distinct automated-reasoning route, not as a reduction in difficulty.

steps.formal_statement: Define the shortcut map T and the 11-rule mixed binary-ternary string rewriting system R_T=D_T union X, with nine value-preserving auxiliary rules and two right-terminal dynamic rules.
steps.lean_style: def yahSystem : StringRewriteSystem MixedDigit := dynamicRules ∪ auxiliaryRules

steps.formal_statement: For every rewrite N -> N', an auxiliary step preserves Val(N), while a dynamic step satisfies Val(N')=T(Val(N)); the unique representation of 1 is irreducible.
steps.lean_style: theorem yah_step_semantics (h : Rewrite yahSystem N N') : (AuxiliaryStep h → value N' = value N) ∧ (DynamicStep h → value N' = shortcutT (value N)) := by ...

steps.formal_statement: Auxiliary-only rewriting terminates, and it suffices to test termination from canonical delimiter strings. Hence an infinite full derivation must contain infinitely many dynamic steps.
steps.lean_style: theorem yah_auxiliary_normalization : StronglyNormalizing auxiliaryRules ∧ (TerminatesOnCanonical yahSystem → StronglyNormalizing yahSystem) := by ...

steps.formal_statement: The full system R_T is terminating if and only if every positive integer reaches 1 under the shortcut Collatz map T.
steps.lean_style: theorem yah_simulation_equivalence : StronglyNormalizing yahSystem ↔ Collatz := by ...

steps.formal_statement: Let E be the exceptional odd terminal rule and R_0=R_T minus E. The system R_0 terminates. On canonical strings it has a unique normal form, and one E-step followed by R_0-normalization is one accelerated odd Collatz step, independent of the normalization schedule.
steps.lean_style: theorem yah_deleted_system_and_macrostep : StronglyNormalizing R0 ∧ UniqueCanonicalNormalForm R0 ∧ ExceptionalMacrostep R0 E = acceleratedOddMap := by ...

steps.formal_statement: Prove relative termination SN(E rel R_0): no infinite R_T derivation applies the exceptional rule E infinitely often.
steps.lean_style: theorem exceptional_rule_relative_termination : RelativelyStronglyNormalizing E R0 := by -- OPEN

steps.formal_statement: YAH-05 and YAH-06 imply termination of R_T by rule removal; YAH-04 then yields the ordinary Collatz conjecture.
steps.lean_style: theorem collatz_of_exceptional_relative_termination (hE : RelativelyStronglyNormalizing E R0) : Collatz := yah_simulation_equivalence.mp (ruleRemoval hE yah_deleted_system_and_macrostep.1)

skeletons.name: Finite residue-cylinder descent cover
skeletons.sufficiency: Closing OPEN-DESCENT-COVER-01 yields a checked descent below every starting value; the stopping-time equivalence and strong induction then prove the ordinary Collatz conjecture.
skeletons.warning: A finite universal descent cover is stronger than Collatz and is not known to exist. Its attraction is certificateability: a proposed cover can be checked by finite exact arithmetic.

steps.formal_statement: Collatz is equivalent to the finite-descent property that every integer n>1 has some iterate T^k(n)<n.
steps.lean_style: theorem collatz_iff_eventual_descent : Collatz ↔ ∀ n > 1, ∃ k, iterate shortcutT k n < n := by ...

steps.formal_statement: Each finite shortcut-parity word determines one residue class modulo a power of 2, and the corresponding iterate is affine on that class; uniform descent and its finite exceptional range are decidable by exact integer arithmetic.
steps.lean_style: theorem parity_cylinder_affine (w : ParityWord) : ∃ r c s, ∀ n ∈ cylinder w, 2^w.length * iterate shortcutT w.length n = 3^s * n + c := by ...

steps.formal_statement: Known strongly sufficient residue sets constrain every hypothetical divergent orbit or nontrivial cycle, and finite verification discharges all seeds below 2^71; these facts may prune a cover but do not make it universal.
steps.lean_style: theorem known_descent_cover_constraints : StronglySufficient (residue 2 9) ∧ BadOrbitHits (residue 20 27) ∧ VerifiedBelow (2^71) := by ...

steps.formal_statement: Construct a finite family of parity/residue cylinders covering every n>1, each equipped with a checked finite iterate that is uniformly below n after explicitly discharging its bounded exceptional representatives.
steps.lean_style: theorem finite_universal_descent_cover : ∃ C : Finset DescentCylinder, CoversPositiveAboveOne C ∧ ∀ c ∈ C, CheckedUniformDescent c := by -- OPEN

steps.formal_statement: RDC-04 gives eventual descent for every n>1; RDC-01 then proves Collatz by strong induction.
steps.lean_style: theorem collatz_of_finite_descent_cover (h : FiniteUniversalDescentCover) : Collatz := collatz_iff_eventual_descent.mpr (descent_of_cover h)

skeletons.name: q-series conjugacy and polynomiality
skeletons.sufficiency: Closing OPEN-QPOLY-01 places every positive integer, through a genuine dynamical conjugacy, inside the completely classified polynomial dynamics of T_{1,1+q^2}; conjugacy then proves the ordinary Collatz conjecture.
skeletons.warning: Monks proves that the polynomiality gate is equivalent to Collatz. The q-series model supplies a useful no-carry representation and a strict polynomial-degree descent, but it does not reduce the logical difficulty until polynomiality of H(n) is proved for the actual conjugacy.

steps.formal_statement: Define the shortcut map T on Z_2 and the family T_{A,B} on F_2[[q]], with division by q in the even branch and (Af+B)/q in the odd branch, for odd A and B.
steps.lean_style: def qAnalog (A B : F2PowerSeries) (hA : Odd A) (hB : Odd B) : F2PowerSeries → F2PowerSeries := fun f => if Even f then f / q else (A*f+B) / q

steps.formal_statement: For every odd A,B in F_2[[q]], the dynamical system T_{A,B} is conjugate to the shortcut Collatz map T on Z_2.
steps.lean_style: theorem monks_q_conjugacy (hA : Odd A) (hB : Odd B) : ∃ H : Z2 ≃ F2PowerSeries, H ∘ shortcutT = qAnalog A B ∘ H := by ...

steps.formal_statement: For Q=T_{1,1+q^2}, an input is a polynomial if and only if its image under Q is a polynomial; every polynomial orbit strictly descends in degree until it reaches the 2-cycle {1,q} or the fixed points 0 and 1+q.
steps.lean_style: theorem selected_q_polynomial_dynamics : (Polynomial f ↔ Polynomial (Q f)) ∧ (Polynomial f → EventuallyIn (orbit Q f) ({1,q} ∪ {0,1+q})) := by ...

steps.formal_statement: For any conjugacy H between T and Q, a positive integer n has a T-orbit containing 1 if and only if H(n) is a polynomial. The fixed-point alternatives cannot correspond to positive integer T-orbits.
steps.lean_style: theorem reaches_one_iff_conjugate_polynomial (H : Conjugacy shortcutT Q) (n : PositiveInt) : Reaches shortcutT n 1 ↔ Polynomial (H n) := by ...

steps.formal_statement: For a conjugacy H between T and T_{1,1+q^2}, H(n) is a polynomial for every positive integer n.
steps.lean_style: theorem positive_integers_have_polynomial_q_images (H : Conjugacy shortcutT Q) : ∀ n : PositiveInt, Polynomial (H n) := by -- OPEN

steps.formal_statement: QPOLY-04 and QPOLY-05 imply that every positive integer reaches 1 under T, hence prove the ordinary Collatz conjecture.
steps.lean_style: theorem collatz_of_q_polynomiality (hPoly : ∀ n : PositiveInt, Polynomial (H n)) : Collatz := fun n => (reaches_one_iff_conjugate_polynomial H n).mpr (hPoly n)
